**4B.6 Research Note: Andrés Manuel López Obrador (2024)**

**Bottom line:** negative overall. I found one clear positive signal that an independent court forced a reply right, but the stronger 2024 record is hostile rhetoric toward journalists, doxxing/intimidation, weak protection for reporters, and surveillance/transparency concerns.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| México | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/mexico | The Reuters Institute says Gálvez obtained a court-ordered right of reply to AMLO’s false claims. This is limited positive evidence that independent institutions could still protect information access against presidential abuse. | 4B.6, 4B.4 |
| 20.05.24 Versión estenográfica de la conferencia de prensa matutina del presidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador | Presidencia de México | 2024-05-20 | https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/20-05-24-version-estenografica-de-la-conferencia-de-prensa-matutina-del-presidente-andres-manuel-lopez-obrador/ | AMLO said conservatives were “adversaries, not enemies” and that repression, authoritarianism, and censorship were unnecessary. This is weak but real rhetorical counterevidence to a blanket censorship posture. | 4B.6, 4B.5, 4B.3 |
| México | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/mexico | The Reuters Institute described AMLO’s final year as marked by continued verbal attacks on journalists, human-rights advocates, and the media. This is negative evidence of a hostile environment for independent media. | 4B.6, 3B.3, 4B.3, 4B.5 |
| Mexico | Reuters via Yahoo News Canada | 2024-02-26 | https://ca.news.yahoo.com/mexicos-president-defends-decision-share-174417727.html | AMLO publicly displayed a New York Times journalist’s phone number and defended the move. That is direct intimidation of a critical journalist. | 4B.6, 3B.3, 4B.3, 4B.5 |
| Mexico | Amnesty International / CPJ | 2024-03-06 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/mexico-killings-journalists-strengthen-federal-mechanism/ | Amnesty and CPJ reported that journalists enrolled in the federal protection mechanism were still being killed, showing the state was not reliably protecting investigative journalism. | 4B.6, 3B.7, 3B.8, 4B.3 |
| México | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/mexico/freedom-net/2024 | Freedom House says the government used insecurity to justify expanding state surveillance with little accountability, and that a covert SEDENA cyberspace unit monitored critics using inauthentic accounts. This is strong negative evidence for pressure and surveillance on information space. | 4B.6, 4B.5, 4B.2 |
| Mexico proposed constitutional changes threaten rights | Human Rights Watch | 2024-08-30 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/30/mexico-proposed-constitutional-changes-threaten-rights | HRW warned AMLO’s proposed constitutional changes could erode privacy and transparency safeguards. That is negative evidence against protecting information access and independent scrutiny. | 4B.6, 4B.4, 4B.5, 4B.2 |

**Search gap:** I found little direct 2024 evidence of formal state propaganda campaigns or explicit censorship orders. The strongest available evidence is instead about intimidation, hostile rhetoric, surveillance, and weak protection for journalists.
